newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish banks' assets rose in first-half 1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkish banks' assets rose in first-half 1996.

text.p: Turkish banking assets grew by 15 percent in real terms in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year, the Turkish Banks Association said in a report.

"Turkish banks' consolidated balance sheets rose by 102 percent to 5,626 trillion lira in January-June this year from same period last year. But when compared with wholesale price indices, the growth was only 15 percent," the report said.
It added consolidated balance sheets grew by nine percent in dollar terms to $68.6 billion over the same periods.
In the first half of 1996, banks' total net profits reached 54 trillion lira, up only eight percent from first half 1995.
Wholesale prices increased 43.7 percent in the first half of 1996 and 76.2 percent year-on-year in June.

The report said, shares of state and foreign banks in total bank assets dwindled in the year to June 1996 while private banks' share rose to 52 percent from 49 percent in June 1995. State banks' share in total assets fell to 38 percent from 40 and foreign banks' share was halved to two percent.
Shares of development and investment banks' assets in the banking sector were steady at 7 percent over the same period.

Total deposits expanded 24 percent from a year ago to 3,785 trillion lira annually in June 1996. A real increase of 35 percent in foreign currency deposits was recorded while lira deposits rose by 14 percent.
